andijan: In the January 1997 RADARSAT-1 frame the dark water fills a wider reservoir whose eastern arm reaches farther east than in the late-October 2026 NISAR frame; the level swings with the season, so this is two dates, not a trend.
tashkent: The same main features sit in both frames (the airport runway south of centre, the dark strip on the east edge, the bright dense centre); city growth since 1999 cannot be separated from the C-band vs L-band difference at this scale.
aral: In July 1997 smooth open water covers the western two-thirds of the box up to a sharp eastern shore; in October 2026 the same area shows land texture everywhere, with the long island's outline now sitting in dry seabed and a straight track crossing where the water was.
urmia: The island and the causeway line are the same in both; in 1999 dark water ends at a sharp eastern shore, while in 2026 the dark area runs past that old shore, and dark L-band can be water or a smooth dry salt bed, so these two radar images alone do not show how much water is left.
